capability.name: Building and versioning Policy Plus
capability.purpose: Stamp the program with its current Git version when it is built.

layers.name: Build tooling
layers.purpose: Scripts a developer runs outside the program to prepare it for compiling, such as stamping the build with its version.

actions.name: version.bat
actions.purpose: Rewrites the generated version file so the program carries the current Git commit description.

context.scope: Action started by a person of Building and versioning Policy Plus: Rewrites the generated version file so the program carries the current Git commit description.
rules: When the build script runs, it replaces the program's version in a generated source file with the text git gives for the current commit. That text is a tag, commit count and short commit name when tags exist, and a short commit name otherwise. The script runs when someone runs it or the release workflow does. The committed file holds an empty version. (version.bat:1)
unconfirmed: For the capability: The build script puts git's text between two quote marks on separate lines of the generated file. We assume the file is still valid code and the version string works. If wrong: The build would fail or embed a wrong version after the script runs.
context.commit: not recorded: the folder was not a git repository
